findings.title: ECS task role has wildcard S3 permissions
findings.description: Task role 'ecommerce-task-role' grants s3:* on all buckets. Violates least-privilege principle. Overly broad S3 permissions are exploitable via SSRF or container breakout.
findings.remediation: Restrict to specific actions (s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject) on specific bucket ARNs.
findings.chain_correlation: Related to Chain 6 and Chain 16 blast radius. Posture finding only -- attack chain not modeled.

findings.title: ECS task environment variable contains potential secret (HF_TOKEN)
findings.description: ECS task definition 'techstride-inference' contains environment variable 'HF_TOKEN' in plaintext. Secrets in task definition environment variables are visible in CloudTrail, ECS DescribeTaskDefinition API, and console. Should be stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
findings.remediation: Store HF_TOKEN in AWS Secrets Manager. Reference via secrets block in task definition.
findings.chain_correlation: WCSPM-4472 identifies the credential exposure posture. The downstream attack -- CI compromise exfiltrates HF_TOKEN, attacker pushes malicious modeling_product_recommender.py, trust_remote_code=True executes it on restart -- is a multi-system attack chain not modeled by CSPM posture evaluation.

findings.title: S3 bucket has public-read ACL
findings.description: S3 bucket 'techstride-export-results-prod' is configured with ACL public-read. All objects are accessible without authentication. Export files containing customer order data are exposed.
findings.remediation: Remove public-read ACL. Serve exports via presigned URLs with TTL.
findings.chain_correlation: R-Chain 8 artifact. UUID job IDs remediated the BOLA but public S3 ACL left all exports accessible via direct URL.

findings.title: ECS task role accumulates secretsmanager:GetSecretValue across multiple secrets
findings.description: Task role 'ecommerce-task-role' has been granted secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on 4 secrets (redis-auth-token, supplier-hmac-secret, stripe-secret-key, db-connection-string) across separate IAM policy updates. Role blast radius grows with each sprint.
findings.remediation: Implement per-service IAM roles. Each ECS service should have a task role scoped only to the secrets it requires.
findings.chain_correlation: Architectural posture finding. Corresponds to the systemic pattern documented in demo-all-chains-2: SSRF-accessible ECS credentials accumulate Secrets Manager permissions with each remediation sprint. Wiz CSPM correctly identifies the policy accumulation. The attack chain -- Chain 6 SSRF -> ECS creds -> GetSecretValue on any of these 4 secrets -- is not surfaced as a connected finding.

findings.title: JWT secret uses weak default value path
findings.description: IaC for ECS task definition references ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET with a fallback pattern that may resolve to a predictable value if the environment variable is unset in some deployments.
findings.remediation: Enforce ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET via Secrets Manager. Remove fallback value in application code.

summary.chain16_note: WCSPM-4472 correctly flags HF_TOKEN as a secrets posture violation (HIGH). CSPM evaluates individual resource configurations against policy rules. The supply chain attack -- CI compromise exfiltrates HF_TOKEN, malicious model pushed to HuggingFace, trust_remote_code=True executes payload on next inference container restart -- spans GitHub Actions, an external ML registry, and ECS runtime. This cross-system attack chain is outside the scope of cloud posture management tools. Posture finding is real and correct. Attack chain is invisible to the tool.
